title: Social Media Privacy Settings: Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp
html:
Privacy on social apps comes down to four questions. Who can see what you post? Who can contact you? What do you show without meaning to, such as when you were last online? And how hard is it for someone to take over the account? Check each one on the apps you use, starting with the account that has the most about you.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. Apps move their settings often. Search for a setting's name inside the app, and use the platform's help centre (linked below) for the current path.

I checked these settings on my own phone (vivo V23 Pro, Android 14) on 11 Oct 2026 and changed nothing. The exact menu paths for Instagram, WhatsApp and Facebook are in the section "Where these settings are on my phone", near the end.

1. Decide who can see your posts

  • Instagram: a private account means people must request to follow you, and your posts go only to approved followers. Also check who can see your stories.
  • Facebook: run the Privacy Checkup, and set the default audience for new posts. Check old posts and your profile details.
  • WhatsApp: your profile photo, About and Last seen can each be limited, for example to your contacts only.

2. Decide who can contact you

Look at who can message you, who can add you to groups, who can tag or mention you, and who can comment. For each, choose the narrowest option you can live with. Being added to a group by strangers can be a way for scammers to reach you, so set the groups option to contacts only if it is offered.

3. Check what you show without posting

Instagram's Activity Status shows other people when you were last active. Instagram's help page describes the setting as "Show Activity Status" under the messages settings: if you turn it off, you also stop seeing other people's status. WhatsApp has the same idea in "Last seen and online". It is a convenience setting, so turn it off if you do not want to be tracked by it.

4. Lock the account itself

A privacy setting does not help if someone logs in as you. Use a strong password that you use nowhere else, and turn on two-factor authentication on every social account. See our guide to two-factor authentication. If a code arrives that you did not ask for, read what an unrequested OTP means and never share it with a caller. Never read out a verification code to anyone, including a caller who claims to be from WhatsApp, a bank or a delivery company.

Review the places the account is signed in, and sign out any device you do not recognise. Remove apps and websites you connected to the account and no longer use.

5. What not to post

  • Documents, tickets or cards, even partly hidden.
  • Your exact home address or a live location. Post a place after you leave it.
  • Photos that show a house number, a number plate or a school uniform.
  • Anything you use as a security answer, such as a pet's name or your mother's maiden name.

A scam message from a "friend" or a fake profile can look real. Our phishing guide shows what to check before you click or reply.

Where these settings are on my phone

Instagram (version 450.0.0.50.77)

My account is public, so I did not make it private. The paths are:

  • Private account: Profile, menu, Settings and activity, Who can see your content, Account privacy, then the Private account switch.
  • Activity status: Settings and activity, How others can interact with you, Messages and story replies, Who can see you're online, Show activity status. Show read receipts is on the same screen.
  • Who can message you: the same Messages and story replies screen, under How people can reach you, Message requests. Story replies is next to it.
  • Tags: Settings and activity, How others can interact with you, Tags and mentions.

WhatsApp (version 2.26.38.73)

Tap You at the bottom right, then Privacy. That screen has Last seen and online, Profile picture, About, Status, Read receipts, Groups, Calls (with Silence unknown callers) and App lock. On mine, Last seen and online, Profile picture and Status are set to exclude chosen contacts.

Facebook (website)

I checked Facebook on the website in a desktop browser, not in the phone app, so I cannot give an app version or an app menu path. The Privacy Checkup page is at facebook.com/privacy/unified_checkup. It shows five topics: Who can see what you share, How people can find you on Facebook, Your data settings on Facebook, How to keep your account secure, and Your ad preferences on Facebook.

What to do next

  1. Pick the account that has the most about you and go through sections 1 to 3.
  2. Turn on two-factor authentication on each social account.
  3. Do a yearly check of connected apps and logged-in devices.

Sources

  • Turn your Instagram Activity Status on or off (Instagram Help Center)
  • Instagram Help Center
  • Facebook Help Centre
  • WhatsApp Help Centre
